# 1 Samuel Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 151 | **Source Image:** 1SA_001_page_001.jpg, 1SA_001_page_002.jpg

---

**1** There was a certain man from Ramathaim-zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite.

**2** And he had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the second was Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

**3** And this man would go up from his city year by year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of hosts at Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the LORD there.

**4** And on the day when Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters.

**5** But to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved Hannah, though the LORD had closed her womb.

**6** And her rival would provoke her bitterly, so as to make her fret, because the LORD had closed her womb.

**7** And so it was year by year; as often as she went up to the house of the LORD, so she would provoke her. And she wept and would not eat.

**8** And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"

**9** And Hannah rose after eating and after drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting upon his seat by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.

**10** And she was bitter of soul, and she prayed to the LORD and wept greatly.

**11** And she vowed a vow and said, "O LORD of hosts, if you will indeed look upon the affliction of your maidservant and remember me and not forget your maidservant, but will give to your maidservant a son, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall come upon his head."

**12** And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the LORD, that Eli watched her mouth.

**13** Now Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. And Eli thought her to be drunk.

**14** And Eli said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine from you."

**15** And Hannah answered and said, "No, my lord, I am a woman hard-pressed in spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.

**16** Do not regard your maidservant as a worthless woman, for out of the abundance of my anxiety and my vexation I have spoken until now."

**17** And Eli answered and said, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him."

**18** And she said, "Let your maidservant find favour in your eyes." And the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.

**19** And they rose early in the morning and worshipped before the LORD, and they returned and came to their house in Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her.

**20** And it came to pass at the turn of days that Hannah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Samuel, saying, "Because I asked him of the LORD."

**21** And the man Elkanah went up, and all his household, to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and his vow.

**22** But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, "Not until the child is weaned; then I will bring him, that he may appear before the LORD and remain there forever."

**23** And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Do what is good in your eyes. Remain until you have weaned him; only may the LORD establish his word." So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.

**24** And she brought him up with her when she had weaned him, with three bulls and one ephah of flour and a skin of wine, and she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh. And the child was young.

**25** And they slaughtered the bull and brought the child to Eli.

**26** And she said, "O my lord! As your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you, praying to the LORD.

**27** For this child I prayed, and the LORD has granted me my petition that I asked of him.

**28** And I also have lent him to the LORD; all the days that he lives he is lent to the LORD." And he worshipped the LORD there.

---

## LOGOS Translation Notes

1. **"Ramathaim-zophim"** (v. 1): Retained the full Hebrew place name (הָרָמָתַיִם צוֹפִים) rather than shortening to "Ramah," as the Leningrad text preserves the dual form. The shorter "Ramah" appears in v. 19 as the domestic residence.

2. **"Double portion"** (v. 5): The Hebrew מָנָה אַחַת אַפָּיִם is literally "one portion of the face/nostrils." The meaning is debated -- it may signify a "worthy portion" or a "double portion." The formal rendering "double portion" follows the traditional understanding that Elkanah gave Hannah a preferential share.

3. **"Bitter of soul"** (v. 10): Rendered literally from מָרַת נָפֶשׁ. The phrase preserves the Hebrew idiom connecting emotional anguish directly to the nefesh (soul).

4. **"Hard-pressed in spirit"** (v. 15): Hebrew קְשַׁת רוּחַ -- literally "hard/difficult of spirit." This maintains the formal register of Hannah's self-description before the priest.

5. **"I asked him of the LORD"** (v. 20): The name שְׁמוּאֵל (Samuel) is connected by the narrator to the verb שָׁאַל (to ask). The etymology reflects the narrative theology: the child's very name testifies to answered prayer.

6. **"Lent him to the LORD"** (v. 28): Hebrew הִשְׁאִלְתִּהוּ -- from the same root שׁאל as Samuel's name. Hannah's wordplay: she "asked" (sha'al) and now "lends back" (hish'il) to the LORD. The formal rendering preserves this verbal connection.

7. **Consistent terms**: "the LORD" for יהוה (YHWH); "soul" for נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh); "spirit" for רוּחַ (ruach); "maidservant" for אָמָה (amah, the more deferential term Hannah uses of herself).

--- LOGOS
